To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
established firms predominantly search broadly and externally when introducing new business model innovations and rely on deep search when innovating processes.

established firms predominantly use several external sources (external search) when introducing a new business model, on internal and extensive external sources with high search intensity (deep search), when innovating processes.

established firms predominantly use several external sources (broads external search) when innovat-ing new business models, internal and external sources (deep search) for process innovations, and broad and deep external sources for product innovations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how established firms search for innovation.
the search behavior of established firms when introducing BMI, products, and processes.
how firms search for innovations and how this search behavior differs between innovation types.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
established firms search broadly for BMI, deeply for process innovation, and broadly and deeply for product innovation.
the innovation process is a multi-dimensional phenomenon that is not fully captured by a one-dimensional approach.
the innovation type (BMI, product or process) and the associated sources of knowledge (internal or external) are important factors to explain how established firms search for innovations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BMI requires a broader search than process and product innovation.
established firms search for BMI differently than for product and process innovation.
established firms should broaden their search when introducing new business model and deepen it when innovating processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BMI is not a single phenomenon but rather a complex set of different types of innovations, each with its own characteristics and associated search behavior.
BMI is a distinct type of innovation that is associated with a different search behavior.
BMI is not a one-size-fits-all solution for established firms.
